ringkasan: Two ESP32 boards connect over the GATT protocol: one acts as the Central, reading a push button, and the other as the Peripheral, turning an LED on or off as soon as it receives a notification.
The delay measured is the one way travel time from Central to Peripheral, compared against the round trip delay the Central prints for itself once the echo comes back.

catatan: Button leg 2 is also tied to GND through a 10 kOhm resistor (pull-down), so GPIO17 reads LOW when the button is not pressed and HIGH when it is.
The LED needs a 220 Ohm current-limiting resistor on its cathode leg so its current stays within the GPIO's safe limit.

persiapan: Selecting the ESP32S3 Dev Module board in the Arduino IDE for both boards (or ESP32 Dev Module if using a DevKit V1)
Changing GROUP_ID in both programs to your group number
Wiring the button's 10 kOhm pull-down resistor and the LED's 220 Ohm current-limiting resistor per the schematic
Syncing both boards' clocks from the same PC
